were exceptionally close to one another, and this has been referred to in the
literature as “Lehmer’s near counterexample” to the Riemann Hypothesis (see
p. 177 of [E]). In our formulation here, those zeros, found by Lehmer, correspond

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Heat-deformed entire functions and the threshold constant
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The Fourier-cosine family H_t converts the real-zero question into a monotone parameter threshold: all zeros are real exactly at and above the de Bruijn–Newman constant, while the Riemann Hypothesis is the assertion that the t=0 member lies on the real-zero side. neighboring_unit_entries.title: Lehmer pairs require a close gap relative to the entire zero environment
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The definition improves on a raw close-pair heuristic: a consecutive simple gap is qualified only when its squared size is small relative to a convergent sum measuring interaction with all other zeros. The discussion explicitly explains that arbitrarily small gaps alone do not suffice.
